mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Shareholder / UBO Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry or competent registrar of the jurisdiction where the direct shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the home jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, the document must be authenticated exclusively by a Hague Apostille issued by the designated competent authority of that home state; the apostilled document is then accepted directly by Korean authorities. If the home jurisdiction is not a member, the document must be consularized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate after prior authentication by the home state's competent foreign affairs authority. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Status Certificate of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or competent government authority of the home jurisdiction of the direct shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route for Apostille Convention states; consular legalization route at the Korean Embassy or Consulate for non-member states. The apostille certificate or the consular legalization certificate is attached to the underlying Certificate of Good Standing; the routes are mutually exclusive and must never be applied in combination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Authorizing Korean Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent or direct shareholder company, duly convened and notarized in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney require a Hague Apostille if executed in an Apostille Convention state, issued by the competent designated authority of the home state; otherwise, after local notarization and home foreign-ministry authentication, the document requires Korean consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive pathways, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and By-Laws of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders, incorporators, or registered agents of the foreign shareholder entity, notarized in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the home jurisdiction has acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention, attach a Hague Apostille issued by the designated competent authority; if not, complete home-state authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Under Korean due diligence practice the document then accompanies the corporate extract and is used without additional Apostille-to-consular chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Shareholder / Funding Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas financial institution holding the shareholder's operating account, signed by the branch manager or compliance officer and notarized in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must carry a Hague Apostille if the bank's home jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; for non-member jurisdictions, it must be authenticated by the home-country foreign-ministry office and then consularized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The Apostille route and consular route are mutually exclusive; the selected single route must be completed before submission to Korean authorities.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, charterers, cargo consignors, consignees, beneficiary banks, and agents are screened prior to onboarding and continuously against Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) suspicious transaction reporting obligations, OFAC SDN/Non-SDN and 13559 lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU and Korean MOFA designations, FATF high-risk countries, and the Korean domestic watch-list. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, foreign public officials, high-risk jurisdictions, and air cargo transshipment corridors. Every match requires corroboration, source-of-funds explanation, senior management approval, and immediate suspicious transaction report to KoFIU where warranted, with all records retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Information System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr and the local district court commercial registration section
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act (Articles 18-24), the statutory corporate name must be written in Korean Hangul, must include the legal-form suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa), and may include an English transliteration in parentheses only when the English name is identical or phonetically equivalent. The four-tier naming convention is: (i) a distinctive principal word; (ii) a business-objective descriptor such as air cargo charter; (iii) the legal-form suffix; and (iv) an optional bracketed English transliteration. Foreign-source names must be transliterated into Hangul and must not create confusion with an identical or highly similar pre-registered name in the same commercial registration jurisdiction or business scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written refusal from the registry court specifying the conflicting name, prohibited token, or missing license. The applicant has 14 days from receipt to file an immediate appeal with the competent district court's commercial registration division, attaching up to three amended alternative names, corrected Hangul transliteration, proof of no identical prior registration, and any ministerial license or approval required for sensitive tokens. The court must decide within 30 days, and if the appeal is rejected again the applicant may file an administrative revocation suit with the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days. Counsel should simultaneously reserve priority under the amended name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Korean Commercial Act and National Tax Service interpretation, a pure virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is rejected as the sole registered office for an air cargo charter broker requiring an air transport business registration under the Aviation Business Act. The seat must be a fixed physical location in Korea, with leased or owned space, a Hangul nameplate, storage of board minutes, contracts, customs air waybills, and actual presence of a domestic director or employee. A serviced suite with dedicated desks and managerial capacity may be accepted by the court and NTS only if the bank also inspects the premises; a mailbox-only address will be rejected by the registry, tax office, and financial institutions and will jeopardize zero-rated VAT treatment and Korean Won settlement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) registered address signboard; (ii) lease agreement or ownership; (iii) on-site board minutes and freight contracts; (iv) air waybill and charter booking ledger; (v) payroll and director presence; (vi) VAT invoice ledger; and (vii) UBO and AML files. Quantified risk is approximately 40-45% within the first 18 months for an air cargo charter broker claiming zero-rated export VAT or using a foreign resident director. The likelihood rises to 60% if customs or red flags arise, if no Korean director is ever physically present, or if the same registered agent hosts more than 10 other companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, applicable sections: Articles 289, 292, 295, 296, 301, 313, 317, 329, 345, 386, 434 and 560; Registration of Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, Articles 193-198; Notary Act, Article 37.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Bureau of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office; for a Seoul-registered Chusik Hoesa this is the Seoul Central District Court Registry, with e-filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System (IREOS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation under Commercial Act Article 317, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, Capital Deposit Certificate, incorporators subscription record, director and auditor consent documents, and statutory attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: South Korean law no longer imposes a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The incorporators may set the initial issued share capital at their discretion, but the subscribed amount must be fully paid and held in a blocked capital-deposit account in the name of the company at a Korean commercial bank until the court registers the incorporation. If foreign investor tax incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act are sought, the foreign investment must total at least KRW 100,000,000 and be reported through KOTRA or an authorized bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION

The undersigned first director(s) of [Company Name], a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, acting without a general meeting in accordance with Article 385 and the applicable provisions of the Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopt the following resolutions effective immediately upon the completion of the incorporation registration:

1. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be established and maintained at [Street Address, City, Republic of Korea]. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the registered office lease, obtain the landlord's consent, file the registered head-office statement with the competent Court Registry, and post any required public notices.

2. Share Capital and Subscription. The authorized capital of the Company is [KRW 5,000,000,000] divided into [50,000,000] ordinary shares with par value KRW 100. The incorporators have subscribed for [10,000] initial ordinary shares with an aggregate issue price of KRW [1,000,000], and the full subscription price shall be paid into a blocked capital-deposit account opened in the name of the Company at [Bank]. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are authorized to present the capital-deposit certificate to the registration officer and to release no funds until the Company receives its certificate of incorporation registration.

3. Banking Authorization. [Bank] is approved as the principal bank of the Company. The Chief Executive Officer, the Managing Director, and such other directors as the Board may designate are authorized, jointly or individually with the limits stated in the corporate seal mandate, to open demand deposit accounts, sign cheques, initiate SWIFT and Fedwire transfers, issue payment instructions, obtain import and export financing and credit lines, and execute any security agreement necessary for banking operations. All banking documents require the corporate seal certificate.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The first Board hereby appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, [Name] as Managing Director, and [Name] as Auditor or, if the Articles provide, an Audit Committee in lieu of a statutory auditor. Each officer shall serve until the first annual general meeting and until a successor is duly appointed. The officers are specifically authorized to sign the incorporation registration application, the business registration filing with the National Tax Service, and the industrial licence application for international air freight forwarding and cargo charter brokerage.

5. General Authorizations. The Representative Director is authorized to register the corporate seal, apply for e-tax invoices, open the corporate tax file, notify foreign investment registration if applicable, and execute all instruments, acknowledgements and verifications necessary to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed under the Notary Act; notarial office in the Seoul Central District Court; for non-resident incorporators, Korean consular or apostille legalization of the power of attorney is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Chusik Hoesa Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the exact corporate name, principal business purpose covering international air freight forwarding and cargo aircraft charter brokerage under ISIC 5229, number and par value of authorized shares, registered head office address, method of public notice, and initial director term. All incorporators must review and execute the articles; the notary verifies identity, legal capacity, subscription declarations, and certifies the articles. For foreign shareholders, the notary should be presented with an apostilled passport or corporate certificate and a notarized power of attorney if the incorporator is represented. Any ambiguity in the business purpose must be corrected before notarization to avoid a registry rejection later.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator
Certificate of foreign legal entity if a corporate incorporator
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if represented
Proof of Korean registered address for the head office if already leased
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification due to identity or document deficiencies, cure the deficiency by submitting an apostilled identity certificate or reappointing a representative with a corrected power of attorney. If the business purpose is too vague, amend the articles to explicitly include international air freight transportation arrangement, cargo charter brokerage, and all ancillary logistics services before re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked escrow verification at a Korean commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized to handle corporate account openings in Korea, ordinarily through the Business Banking Division at a main or corporate branch in Seoul.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, open a temporary paid-in capital account in the corporate name, usually maintained on behalf of the future Chusik Hoesa. Each incorporator transfers the full amount of his or her subscribed capital into this blocked account. The bank verifies subscriber names, remittance amounts, corporate name, and account title, and then issues the Capital Deposit Certificate required under Commercial Act Article 295. The funds must remain frozen or escrowed until the Court Registry issues the certificate of incorporation; after that, the bank releases the funds to the company ordinary operating account upon presentation of the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of subscribers and directors
Passport or foreign corporate certificate for non-resident subscribers
Capital contribution remittance records or deposit slips
Corporate temporary account opening application signed by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a query based on mismatched names, inconsistent remittance amounts, or incomplete beneficial ownership forms, correct the account opening documents, resubmit the subscription record, and request a fresh capital deposit certificate. If deposit funds originated from outside Korea, provide the standard foreign exchange declaration or crypto liquidation records requested by the bank to satisfy anti-money-laundering verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration with the competent Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Bureau of the Seoul Central District Court or the district registry having jurisdiction over the head office, with electronic filing via the Supreme Court of Korea IREOS portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application within two weeks of obtaining the Capital Deposit Certificate. The application must request creation of the corporation and must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, Capital Deposit Certificate, subscriber list and subscription declarations, incorporators meeting minutes or unanimous written consent, director and auditor appointment and acceptance statements, and proof of payment of registration license tax and court fees. The Registry examines whether all Commercial Act formalities have been satisfied, including valid share subscription, minimum capital deposit, director consent and corporate name registrability. Upon approval, the Registry authorizes the company formation and issues the certified copy of the company register and the corporate seal registration certificate, which are the definitive proof of the corporation legal existence.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application form as prescribed by court rules
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital Deposit Certificate issued by the bank
Subscriber list and individual subscription declarations
Minutes of the incorporation meeting or written consent of incorporators
Director and auditor appointment and acceptance documentation
Receipt of payment of registration license tax and court filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a supplementation order, identify the precise defect from the order, file corrected documents immediately within the court-given period, and pay any additional fees. If registration is refused, the incorporators may file an immediate reconsideration motion before the same registry or reapply after remedying the stated irregularities; where the defect concerns the business purpose clause, amend and re-notarize the Articles of Incorporation before the next filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business and tax registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District tax office with jurisdiction over the registered head office; online submission through the National Tax Service Home Tax Service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the certificate of incorporation registration, the company must file a business registration application with the appropriate district tax office. This application establishes the corporate income tax file, value-added tax registration, electronic tax invoice issuance account, and payroll withholding accounts. The corporate seal certificate, lease agreement, articles of incorporation and representative director identity documents are submitted together with the business registration application. The tax office issues the business registration certificate with a unique corporate tax number. The company must also complete the corporation establishment report under the Corporate Tax Act and, if there are foreign shareholders, determine whether a foreign investment report is required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. VAT invoices can only be issued after the business registration certificate is granted.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Lease contract or head-office use consent from the building owner
Representative director and shareholder identity documents
Foreign investment report copy, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or queries the application, file the omitted lease, consents, or representative director authorization and request a provisional tax number while the permanent number is issued. If the electronic tax invoice system cannot be activated, submit the electronic invoice registrant application and provide the business registration certificate; any late-registration fine should be paid promptly in accordance with the tax office assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Air cargo charter brokerage industry licensing and freight forwarder registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT), Civil Aviation Safety Division; delegated service agency Korea International Freight Forwarders Association (KIFFA); customs-related approval from Korea Customs Service where bonded or cargo clearance activity is included.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: To lawfully invoice customers for international air freight forwarding and cargo aircraft charter brokerage services, the company must obtain the appropriate freight forwarder and cargo agent registration before commencing commercial operations. The application is submitted through the designated industry association or MOLIT portal and must demonstrate that the company is a validly incorporated Korean entity with an appropriate business purpose, office space, corporate seal, financial soundness, liability insurance or financial guarantee, and officers without disqualifying criminal records. The company must clearly state that its activities are airway-freight brokerage and charter intermediation, not actual aircraft operation, so no air transport operator certificate is required. After review, the authority issues the operating registration certificate and the company must maintain annual compliance filings, insurance coverage and business reporting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Air freight forwarder or cargo agency application form
Liability insurance policy or financial guarantee certificate
Criminal history certificate for directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Office lease contract and corporate seal certificate
Charter brokerage operating manual and aircraft charter intermediary procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOLIT, KIFFA or the customs service queries the application, remedy the exact insufficiency, usually a missing insurance certificate or a deficient criminal record certificate, and submit a supplementary filing. If the requested license category does not match the actual business model, amend the Articles to include the corrected subcategory and re-file. If any officer is disqualified, appoint a qualified senior manager and update the officer consent forms before resubmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) Civil Aviation Safety Division; delegated licensing agent Korea International Freight Forwarders Association (KIFFA); Korea Customs Service for cargo clearance and bonded compliance matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Air Freight Forwarder Business Registration; where acting as a charter intermediary for cargo aircraft, an Air Cargo Charter Broker Registration and, if dealing with IATA airlines, IATA Cargo Agency Accreditation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Division; technical review by Korea Environment Corporation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for an office-based air cargo charter broker. No industrial construction, manufacturing, chemical processing or warehousing footprint exists at the initial stage; therefore no EIA report or environmental registration is required for the broker license. If the company later adds a physical cargo warehouse, ground handling facility or aircraft maintenance station, a full or small-scale EIA may be triggered, particularly if the planned building floor area is 10,000 m² or more or the site is within an environmental protection zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable at the office-brokerage stage. For any future warehouse or transshipment facility, the following quantitative thresholds would apply: wastewater generation of 50 m³ or more per day requires a wastewater discharge permit under the Clean Water Conservation Act; facilities using 500 m³ per year or more of VOC-containing solvents require Clean Air Conservation Act emission control and stack permits; and generators of more than 100 kg per month of hazardous industrial waste must register under the Wastes Control Act, keep manifests and dispose of waste only through licensed carriers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the administrative office occupancy, the landlord must provide the building fire-fighting and evacuation completion certificate issued under the Firefighting Safety System Act, and the local fire department may inspect the premises. The company must file a workplace commencement report with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, provide safety signage, and complete mandatory annual health and safety training for all employees. If a cargo warehouse is later added, a separate fire safety permit and dangerous goods storage license would be required, including structural load inspection and hazardous chemical compliance under the Korea Gas Safety Act and Emergency and Safety Management Act; for pure office brokerage, no civil defense or fire-site permit is otherwise required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); online electronic portal: HomeTax electronic taxation service (www.hometax.go.kr). Export customs declarations are processed by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa with a domestic place of business: (1) complete corporate incorporation at the commercial registry; (2) file the standard business registration application with the competent NTS district tax office within 20 days of opening the business; (3) NTS will issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified tax identification number for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding tax, and e-Tax Invoice purposes. Required evidence includes certified articles of incorporation, corporate registry excerpt, proof of registered office and actual place of business, business opening details, and the representative director's identification. For a non-resident foreign entity with no Korean place of business: (1) use the English-language HomeTax non-resident simplified VAT registration service; (2) upload the foreign incorporation certificate, tax residence certificate, bank proof, electronic contact details, and a power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative or certified tax accountant where required; (3) receive the assigned simplified VAT ID / business number for filing Korean VAT on Korean-sourced supplies; (4) if exporting goods or operating specialized air-cargo brokerage, also obtain the necessary Korea Customs Service entity registration or customs ID and register the export-related business activity. All TIN issuance is subject to NTS verification; no fictional or provisional TIN is recognized.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea provides no elective check-the-box classification for a Chusik Hoesa, nor does it allow an elective hybrid-mismatch regime; tax classification is prescribed by law and anti-hybrid rules are mandatory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for domestic taxable persons; registration is mandatory from business commencement. For non-resident electronic-service or offshore suppliers, nexus is based on Korean consumer location; simplified VAT registration is mandatory when supplying taxed electronic services to Korean recipients, and actual returns report only Korean-source taxable turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every VAT-registered Korean business supplier, including an export-oriented air-cargo charter broker, must issue an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) through the NTS HomeTax platform or an NTS-integrated accounting/ERP API and transmit it to NTS by the day after the supply. Paper invoices are not acceptable for input VAT credit. Korea does not use physical fiscal stamping; anti-fraud digital control is implemented through centralized NTS real-time invoice registration, mandatory periodic VAT return reconciliation, and the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declaration interface.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Korean VAT Act applies to exports of goods physically removed from Korea and to services, including brokerage and freight-forwarding services, that are directly ancillary to such exports, supplied to non-resident parties, and paid for in foreign currency. An air-cargo charter broker must demonstrate that the commission or brokerage fee arises from an international air-transport/cargo-charter transaction for goods exported from Korea, that the service recipient is a foreign enterprise or a designated non-resident party, and that the service is actually performed in connection with the export movement. Certain qualifying services supplied electronically to non-resident customers may also be zero-rated where the place of supply rules place the service outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration transmitted through UNI-PASS and certified by Korea Customs Service (export clearance confirmation for physical outbound air cargo)
Commercial invoice and the cargo charter agreement or international freight forwarding contract naming the Korean exporter, foreign consignee, and the international flight/cargo service
Bill of Lading (for sea legs) or Air Waybill (Master and/or House) showing pickup in Korea and delivery outside Korea, including flight numbers, cargo description, and consignee details

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Korean Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency payment, supported by SWIFT wire or Fedwire remittance advices
Service completion or delivery confirmation proving the cross-border service was actually performed, such as destination customs entry, delivery receipt, or release instruction
Corporate and VAT identity evidence, including the Business Registration Certificate and the e-Tax Invoice, confirming the legal supplier and that no separate domestic VAT was charged
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS may cross-check export e-Tax Invoices with UNI-PASS customs declarations, signed waybills, and bank foreign-exchange records during post-clearance VAT audits. If the zero-rated export cannot be substantiated, the 10% VAT is assessed and collected with statutory interest and penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act. Willfully false zero-rating or fabricated customs and foreign-exchange documentation triggers criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including fines, imprisonment, loss of tax advantages, full retrospective clawback of any refunded VAT, and debarment from export-related tax relief. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days without an approved extension similarly attracts foreign-exchange penalties unless the amount is lawfully exempted or re-imported.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, supported by the Korea Customs Service for trade declarations and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) for reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is generally convertible on the current account for bona fide trade, service fees, and dividend remittances, but capital account transactions remain strictly controlled under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Non-resident equity investments, cross-border loans, and repatriation of principal investment proceeds require prior reporting or approval through a designated foreign exchange bank. Export proceeds must be received and surrendered into a domestic foreign currency account or converted into won within prescribed deadlines; a substantial portion of export earnings is subject to mandatory conversion into KRW under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act relevant subordinate regulations. For a Korea inbound foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa engaged in air cargo charter broking, profit repatriation and capital redemptions are permissible after corporate tax clearance, external audit where applicable, and submission of the required Foreign Exchange Transactions Report to the Bank of Korea via the designated bank. Practical hurdles include documentary verification of the underlying commercial transactions, anti-money laundering checks on counterparties across multiple jurisdictions, and the requirement to prove that remitted funds originate from legitimate operating revenues rather than disguised capital flows. The Corporate body must maintain accurate foreign exchange transaction ledgers and file month-by-month BOK reports for each foreign exchange position above statutory thresholds. Because Korea applies a negative-list capital account regime, transactions not expressly restricted can proceed through reporting, but any deviation from the declared business purpose is treated as unauthorized foreign exchange trading and can trigger monetary penalties. Thus the treasury blueprint must embed transaction purpose codes, underlying invoices, and contemporaneous compliance documentation at every wire point.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be collected within a statutory period of 6 months from the export declaration date, subject to extension for justified trade terms, and the exporter must convert or surrender such receipts into won through a designated foreign exchange bank on or before the due date. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% of export proceeds, except where explicitly exempted under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, for example certain intercompany settlement flows or insured export receivables that qualify for retention in a foreign currency account after obtaining approval from the designated bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted. Offshore digital EMI providers are not permitted to act as the primary clearing or settlement bank for restructuring-oriented entities in Korea because corporate account registration must be held with an institution licensed under the Korean Banking Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A foreign fintech EMI may operate only as a compliant technology vendor intermediated by a domestic licensed bank, and it cannot open domestic won settlement accounts, issue Korean IBAN corporate facilities, or independently process BOK foreign exchange reporting. Any unlicensed solicitation or EMI wallet-based movement of incoming equity capital in KRW would be deemed unauthorized foreign exchange brokerage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the authorised signatory or a statutory director at the branch during the initial corporate account opening interview. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted only where the non-resident director executes a notarised and apostilled power of attorney at the Korean consulate specifying the specific branch, account class, and transaction patterns; the appointed proxy must still appear in-person at the bank with the original corporate registration documents and the director's certified identity file. For enhanced risk sectors such as air cargo charter broking, banks frequently require the actual legal representative to appear once, either under non-face-to-face video KYC for low-risk profiles or physically for the final signing, to affirm beneficial ownership and intended business activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership ambiguity caused by non-resident shareholders masking their identity in the Chusik Hoesa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised certificate of corporate registration in Korea, apostilled notarised passports of all shareholders, shareholder registry with proportional ownership, source-of-wealth statements, bank reference letters from the home jurisdiction, and a signed UBO declaration in compliance with the Financial Action Task Force and Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Air cargo charter broker activity not matching the stated business purpose at account activation because freight forwarding and charter broking have broad ancillary structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid air freight forwarder registration certificate, aircraft charter brokerage agreements, capacity purchase contracts with airlines, operational flow chart showing money settling versus chartered cargo, and a written compliance explanation that the account is not used for personal transit of aircraft or third-party fund transit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction counterparties hidden within charter payment chains for cargo movements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated and manual sanctions screening logs for all counterparties, full beneficial ownership records of charter counterparties, contracted air cargo invoices with complete flight and consignment numbers, UBO certifications from wholesalers, and a corporate transaction monitoring policy covering red flags such as unusual cash payments, split transactions, and abrupt rerouting of charter fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound and outbound FX wires showing mismatch of transaction purpose codes and underlying trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter agreements linking the bank transfer to the cargo route and flight number, invoices and payment schedules, customs export and import declarations, BOK foreign exchange reporting form, and an external auditor's report confirming the economic substance and valuation of each cross-border disbursement before the bank's compliance committee approves high-risk payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injection must be routed via SWIFT wire to the designated domestic commercial bank under the foreign exchange bank's capital account registration. The bank will issue a certificate of receipt, and the non-resident shareholder must submit the Korean-styled report of acquisition of shares to the Bank of Korea within the statutory window. The treasurer must use the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code for equity investment in a Korean corporation, usually 004003 for acquisition of shares by a non-resident investor, and maintain the source-of-funds documentation. Upon receipt the funds are held in a capital escrow account until a certified capital verification report is issued by an external auditor confirming actual cash contribution. The Chusik Hoesa then transfers the funds into the operational KRW account, distinct from the foreign currency settlement account, and each subsequent transfer must be internally matched against the corporate ledger to prove the equity capital was not diverted into trade finance speculation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for aircraft charter payments must use SWIFT MT103 for unambiguous prime beneficiary wire settlement, with full documentary records attached to the instruction. Larger contractual periodic block-charter or ACMI payments are better executed through an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the Korean bank and advised to the foreign airline or charter broker, ensuring reconciliation against an aircraft charter agreement that includes tail number identification, crew and maintenance operating scope, and delivery and redelivery dates. For lower-value but recurrent handling, fuel invoices, and ground handling costs, documentary collections can be used where the bank transmits transport documents through the correspondent banking network and releases documents against payment. Every outbound remittance must carry a precise foreign exchange bank purpose code, and the physical or electronic copy of the underlying invoice must be archived for five years to withstand BOK and tax audits. For high-value USD wires settling via Fedwire and SWIFT, the Korean bank may impose a pre-screening hold until the charter party's FATC status under Korean anti-money laundering guidance is confirmed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Korean won forward contracts permitted for hedging committed air cargo receivables and payables denominated in major foreign currencies

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for speculating or hedging offshore won exposure only when executed through domestic licensed banks and supported by physical underlying trade or transaction documentation
Currency swaps for rolling over operational US dollar funding when matched to the contract duration of aircraft charter obligations
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only covering fixed-rate charter-fee loans and subject to BOK foreign exchange position reporting threshold review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (including transfer pricing and foreign tax credit attachments where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Local District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the corporation's main place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligence penalty of up to 20% of unpaid corporate income tax, or 30% for intentional concealment; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% on overdue tax; NTS seizure and collection against corporate bank accounts and trade receivables; criminal referral for tax evasion; administrative strike-off is not automatic, but prolonged dormancy and non-filing can lead to court-ordered dissolution upon creditor, shareholder, or prosecutorial petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Corporate Income Tax Return (semi-annual inter-period payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Local District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the end of the first 6 months of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year corporation, due on or before August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% on the unpaid provisional amount plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%; continued non-compliance is treated as a tax law violation and may expose the company to NTS enforcement and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return (corporate local income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City/province local government with jurisdiction over the corporation's place of business and its nearest local tax collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the corporate income tax return due date; generally April 30 for a calendar-year corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local income tax penalty of up to 20% of unpaid local corporate income tax, 0.022% daily late-payment interest, and enforced collection by local tax authorities; long-term non-payment can result in seizure of assets and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Financial Statements Presentation, Approval, and Statutory Examiner Presentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Shareholders' Meeting (corporate organ); corporate minutes and financial statements must be retained at the head office and made available to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year; ordinary shareholders' meetings are customarily held in March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines on directors and statutory auditors under the Korean Commercial Act of up to KRW 20,000,000 for failure to prepare or present financial statements; failure to hold required meetings can support a court petition to dismiss directors or dissolve the company; no separate government renewal fee is triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to the Financial Supervisory Service and Presentation to Shareholders (for statutory external audit targets)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), particularly the Securities and Futures Commission where the company is subject to external audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be issued before the annual shareholders' meeting and filed with or submitted to the FSS within 2 weeks after the audit report date; financial statements approved by shareholders are subsequently submitted with the audit report where review is ordered.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company and external auditor may each be assessed administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; false or concealed audit reports may result in criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 50,000,000; failure to appoint a certified external auditor when mandated can lead to FSS designation of an auditor and supervisory penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Change Report and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (for foreign shareholders holding or acquiring 10% or more of issued shares)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via KOTRA / Foreign Investment Support Center or designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven, not an annual renewal: report must be made within 30 days after any share transfer, share issuance, capital increase/decrease, merger, or any change in foreign ownership ratio or investment amount; annual onward compliance confirmation is maintained in the corporate secretarial register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report within 30 days is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 3,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may strip the foreign investment of tax support and foreign investment protection until the report is corrected; it does not itself trigger corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa is compulsorily subject to an independent certified CPA audit if it is a stock company listed on a Korean exchange, a public-interest asset-sizable company designated by the Financial Services Commission, or a company whose balance sheet total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000) as of the end of the fiscal year. Korean external audit law does not create a turnover or headcount trigger; however, if the company is foreign-invested, files consolidated financial statements, or engages in designated public-interest activities, audit may also be legally compelled by the relevant disclosure statute. Audits must be performed by an independent certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) under the Korean auditing standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and public-interest entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-public companies not electing K-IFRS; K-IFRS for Small and Medium Enterprises for eligible smaller corporations. External audits are conducted in accordance with Korean Auditing Standards established by KICPA and the FSS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a stand-alone annual UBO registry form for all corporations; instead, the domestic regime is event-driven and bank-verified. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, a foreign investor or a domestic company receiving foreign investment must report the investment to MOTIE or a designated foreign exchange bank, and any shareholding transfer, capital increase, share pledge, or change in foreign ownership ratio must be reported within 30 days. The Financial Transaction Reports Act also requires Korean financial institutions to identify and annually re-verify beneficial owners of corporate clients in connection with real-name verification and anti-money-laundering obligations. The corporate secretarial protocol should therefore include an annual internal UBO confirmation register to evidence foreign ownership ratios, share transfer history, and beneficial ownership for FATF and Korean bank KYC refresh timelines.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 1,500 per year for a Seoul-registered office and professional corporate secretarial agent (KRW 800,000 to KRW 2,000,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National corporate income tax applies at progressive rates of 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on the portion between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion, 21% on the portion between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion, and 24% on the portion exceeding KRW 300 billion; a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax produces an effective headline rate of up to 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in air cargo charter brokerage may qualify under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law for R&D tax credits, temporary facility investment credits, venture and free economic zone incentives, and foreign-investment promotion packages. Qualifying high-tech foreign-invested companies in Free Economic Zones can receive a 100% corporate income tax holiday for 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years, with additional top-up credits for job creation, technology transfer and green logistics investment.
